approach: Re-spec brief delivery on the spawn path in packages/cyberlegion only: the wake carries the instruction to read the brief and begin, replacing the content-free doorbell; the SessionStart hook's spawning->active brief-injection branch is retired as redundant. Mechanism already exists (MuxAdapter.submit/nudge via unit nudge --message) — this is a contract change plus a dead-path retirement, not new plumbing.

Touches mail/surface, unit/lifecycle, mail/doorbell. Expected to narrow frozen scenarios in mail/surface (first-hook-call injects the brief; later call does not re-inject) and unit/lifecycle (brief-by-file, typed launch command carries no brief text; first-turn doorbell block).

Clearance floor GRANTED LIVE by the owner before drafting — the owner was shown the frozen-scenario re-open and the ADR supersession and selected the option naming both. Recorded here per grant-then-record; the narrowing edits follow the spec gate, not this line.
Supersedes ADR-0027 (spawn delivers the first turn), which split payload-delivery from turn-delivery deliberately. The superseding ADR is in this CR, not a follow-up.
leash auto-none: owner is live in-session and both gates are cheap to ratify; emit a verdict and stop at each gate rather than self-assert over a Clearance floor.

Out of scope, filed as follow-ups at handoff: CR-B the cyberlegion-plugin lifecycle abstraction and its frameless-unroutable case; CR-C cyberfleet Operator adopting the seam plus its stale hook prose.

why: Cold sdd-spec-judge round 3 over the re-spec of spawn brief delivery: oracle/builder/architect all PASS, ALIGNED true, SCENARIOS_FAILING [], no blocker, no open markers.
